newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Congo's Kabila leaves Angola after two-day visit.
newsitem.headline: Congo's Kabila leaves Angola after two-day visit.

text.p: Democratic Republic of the Congo President Laurent Kabila left Luanda on Wednesday after two days of talks with Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos and other officials.
Kabila cancelled a scheduled airport press conference, making no comment before leaving for Kinshasa in the Congo, formerly Zaire.

A press release made available by the Angolan Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Kabila had invited dos Santos to visit Kinshasa and that they had reached verbal agreements in areas of cooperation including petroleum, mining, fishing, education, health, culture and transportation.
Kabila held discussions with dos Santos lasting nearly two hours on Tuesday night, Angolan state media reported. On Wednesday, the Congolese leader met Luanda's diplomatic corps.
Diplomats said he spoke mostly about his struggle to topple former Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who was overthrown by rebels led by Kabila in May.

"He talked mostly about the Zairean war. But he also said all the ministers who left the country when Mobutu fell are welcome to come back as long as they bring the money that they stole with them," one diplomat said.

Earlier on Wednesday, UNITA deputies cancelled a meeting of Angola's national assembly that was to have been addressed by Kabila, saying it would be unconstitutional for an elected parliament to meet for an unelected president.

The former rebels are a minority party with 70 seats in the national assembly that they took up earlier this year as part of a three-year-old peace process that ended two decades of civil war against dos Santos' ruling MPLA party.

Diplomats and officials in Luanda said earlier this week dos Santos was expected to ask Kabila to play a vital role in helping the Angolan government deal with UNITA -- once strongly allied to Mobutu. No official comment was forthcoming, however.
